analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md. It bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds a head-side paragraph (around head lines 670-690) describing a new dense-Qwen scheduler behavior: demandedLatestCheckpointMinimumTokens and demandedLatestPromptEndMarginTokens=64. This ends one prefill range at the deepest aligned boundary at least 64 tokens below the prompt end, so a growing conversation's next turn can reuse a deeper checkpoint. I examined the supplied base text (units 2-4) and the patch. Only the base side is visible in full; the new paragraph appears only in the patch excerpt, so I cannot confirm the code. The excerpt is marked incomplete.

Security relevance. T-041 (cross-tenant prefix-cache sharing and TTFT oracle, SEC-035) and TB-007 cover this area. The documented change affects only checkpoint capture geometry. It says the store's existing write gating still applies ('a request the store would write'), fleet-novel refusal is unchanged, and the retained first/target/latest roles and byte limits are unchanged. No change is described to the HMAC lookup tags, the cacheSalt scoping, the DBK3 metadata or AAD, the 30-minute TTL, the disk budget or the KEK wipe. It adds no new on-disk metadata fields and no new plaintext prompt-derived data. It slightly raises checkpoint density and the chance of a hit on the same account, which is the same accepted kind of SEC-035 in-process TTFT oracle, and the per-account salt scoping is unchanged. Write-wear and disk usage stay bounded by the existing three-boundary and byte-admission limits.

Remaining questions for integration: the actual code in EngineV2Factory.demandedLatestCheckpointMinimumTokens and DemandedShortCheckpointRange.swift is not supplied. The doc claim that the 'store would write' gating and the tenant scoping are preserved is therefore unverified. This is a documentation-only diff with no evidence of a regression. I raise no finding and no threat-model update is required.
